faq.q: How much does Faraj Law charge?
faq.a: Faraj Law publishes a contingency fee, which means the fee is a share of what the case recovers and there is nothing to pay if it recovers nothing. The rate itself is not published, so ask for it in writing, along with how case expenses are handled and whether they come out of the recovery before or after the fee. The first consultation is free, which is the place to ask.

faq.q: Does Faraj Law offer a free consultation?
faq.a: Yes. Faraj Law publishes a free initial consultation. It publishes material in Spanish.

faq.q: Where does Faraj Law have offices?
faq.a: Faraj Law publishes two offices, in Chicago and Woodland Hills. Addresses and the Google listing behind each one are on this profile under Offices.

faq.q: Who are the attorneys at Faraj Law?
faq.a: Faraj Law names five attorneys on its own site, and each is listed on this profile with the page we read them from. They have not been checked against a state register: Illinois does not publish an attorney register we can query, so licensure is not verified here. The state's own attorney search is the place to check it.

faq.a: Faraj Law scores 37 and sits at Verified. Passed: website and footprint. Could not be answered from any public source and therefore counts neither for nor against the firm: licensure, discipline and entity registration.
